business_scope.primary_industry_name: Airport Bonded In-Flight Meal Production and Direct Ramp Delivery

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid/Bijural: Quebec private and commercial law follows Civil Law tradition (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991); federal public, criminal, and tax law follows Common Law tradition; enterprise registration and publicity are governed by Quebec civil-code-based statutes.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/ACEUM, in force 1 July 2020)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisionally applicable since 21 September 2017)
Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA, in force 1 January 2015)
Canada-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force 1 October 2014)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 1 April 2021)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by Protocols, including Article XXIX A limitation on benefits)
Canada-France Tax Convention (in force 29 July 1976, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended (imposing 25% beneficial-ownership identification, PEP, and sanctions screening on reporting entities, including Quebec notaries and counsel when receiving funds or giving investment advice); Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c. C-46, ss. 462.3, 462.31, 83.02 and 83.03 (money laundering and terrorist financing offences); Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c. 17 and United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c. U-2 (Canadian autonomous and UN sanctions); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-45 (Quebec enterprise register, declaration of registration for societe en commandite); Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991, arts. 2236-2256 (societe en commandite); Quebec legislation on money-services businesses and anti-money-laundering oversight applicable to financial intermediaries engaged by the partnership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence / Certificate of Good Standing (extrait de registre) of non-resident corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the foreign partner's country of origin (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (Canada acceded effective 11 January 2024; apostille issued by the foreign partner's home-state competent authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (mandat) designating the Quebec-based attorney-in-fact for service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Quebec notary (notaire)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued abroad, or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified and apostilled copies of beneficial owners' passports, photo identification, and proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, attorney, or certified accountant in each owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization in accordance with each country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds letter (attestation de provenance des fonds) for capital contributions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank holding the contributing partner's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature plus Consular Legalization or Apostille as required by the receiving Quebec bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Limited Partnership Deed (contrat de societe en commandite) under Civil Code of Quebec arts. 2236-2256
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec counsel; notarized deed where a partner so requires or where foreign filing standards demand it
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication in Quebec for domestic execution; certified French translation annexed for foreign partners; no apostille required for the domestic deed itself

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-commitment protocol: (i) beneficial-ownership piercing for every natural person holding 25% or more of the partnership, including all general partners and indirect UBOs; (ii) PEP and HEP determination for all partners, officers, and directors in accordance with SOR/2002-184; (iii) screening against the UN Consolidated List, Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, and as prudent market practice the OFAC SDN List; (iv) Criminal Code s. 83.03 terrorist-asset and designated-person verification; (v) continuous adverse-media monitoring with results retained in a FINTRAC-compliant AML file by the Quebec notary or counsel; (vi) prohibition on dealing with blocked persons, designated jurisdictions, or suspect aviation counterparties in the inflight supply chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises, Centre d'acces online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11, arts. 21-26) and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business (CQLR c. C-11, r. 9), every Quebec enterprise name must be in French; a non-French element is admissible only where it is a protected trademark, a personal name, or has no French equivalent. The limited partnership name must close with the French legal designation 'societe en commandite' or the accepted abbreviations 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'. Transliteration of non-Latin scripts is not accepted; names must be rendered in standard Latin-script French spelling with mandatory French designation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms reserved exclusively for incorporated entities ('Inc.', 'Corporation', 'Limited', 'Ltd.') which are incompatible with a societe en commandite
Banking, trust, and insurance terms requiring prior AMF or OSFI clearance ('Bank', 'Banque', 'Trust', 'Fiducie', 'Assurance', 'Pret', 'Caisse')
Professional-title terms restricted to licensed professionals ('Avocat', 'Notaire', 'Medecin', 'Pharmacie' unless duly authorized)
Names identical or phonetically/graphically confusable with any existing name in the REQ database
Vulgar, obscene, or public-order-contravening expressions per REQ administrative practice
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon REQ refusal of a proposed name, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal notice. Within thirty (30) days of refusal, the applicant files a written demand for review (demande de revision) with the Director of the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec pursuant to the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-45), attaching amended name alternatives and legal argument distinguishing existing registered names. If the Director confirms the refusal, an administrative appeal lies to the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within thirty (30) days of the review decision, and ultimate judicial review is available before the Cour superieure du Quebec. The applicant may re-submit a fresh name-reservation file or request a hold while the revision is pending; any pending administrative review suspends the operational naming deadline for incorporation purposes.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible in Quebec only as the declared establishment address for service-of-process and publicity purposes, provided it is a genuine physical address operated by a licensed corporate-services provider that receives documents and maintains corporate records. A purely virtual setup is not acceptable for this industry: an airline inflight catering kitchen requires a fixed, MAPAQ-licensed food-production facility located at or adjacent to the operative airport (e.g., Montreal-Trudeau YUL) with controlled ramp delivery access, bonded storage, and physical kitchen infrastructure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% quantified likelihood of unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first twelve (12) months of operations, comprising MAPAQ sanitary inspections under the Food Products Act (CQLR c. P-29), Canadian Food Inspection Agency verification under the Safe Food for Canadians Act (SC 2012, c. 24), airport security and customs ramp controls, and possible Revenu Quebec payroll/QST field audits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2236–2248 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 12, 17, 22, 23, 29. The Quebec Business Corporations Act does not govern a limited partnership; it may govern a corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Immatriculation Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration for a Québec société en commandite)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement. Limited partners' capital contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement and may be cash, property, or rights; contributions must actually be made before the limited partner may rely on the restriction of liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the general partner of the proposed Quebec limited partnership does hereby: (1) approve and adopt the partnership agreement under Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2248; (2) approve each limited partner’s capital commitment as set out in the capital subscription schedule; (3) authorize the filing of the Déclaration d’immatriculation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; (4) adopt the registered office and partnership domicile specified in that declaration; (5) appoint the general partner as manager, with exclusive authority to bind the partnership and open bank, tax, and catering accounts; and (6) authorize GST/HST and QST registrations and all ancillary documents. This resolution is effective immediately and remains in force until lawfully amended.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec Enterprise Registrar (REQ) – online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform an online name search against the REQ register using the proposed legal name. Ensure the name includes the French legal designation 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' as required by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. If the name is available, pay the reservation fee and obtain a Certificat de réservation de nom valid up to 90 days. Notarization is not required for this step; the submission is electronic.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and legal form wording
Identification details of all general partners
Resolution or authorization if a corporate general partner is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused, the REQ issues a written notice giving reasons such as misleading similarity, prohibited term, or reserved name. File a corrected application with a new distinctive name; the prior refusal does not confer any right to proceed under the refused certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Written Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties themselves; a Quebec notary public if any contribution consists of an immovable or if the partners elect to use an authentic deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign a partnership agreement identifying the limited partnership's name, registered office, general partners with unlimited liability, limited partners with liability restricted to their committed contributions, and each partner's capital contribution. The agreement must comply with Civil Code of Québec arts. 2236–2248. For contributions of immovables, have the agreement notarized and register it in the Quebec land register so that it is opposable to third parties. If the general partner is a legal person, attach its board resolution authorizing execution.
required_dossiers: Entity identification documents for each partner
Board resolution or power of attorney for the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signature is defective, if a partner fails to execute, or if notarization is omitted for an immovable contribution, execute a corrective deed or re-execute the agreement before a notary before filing the declaration. The registry will otherwise reject the declaration at the signature-verification stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec Enterprise Registrar (REQ) – online filing portal, Immatriculation Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration declaration online through the REQ transaction portal. Include the partnership's legal name, full address of the registered office, description of the inflight catering activity, full name and address of the general partner(s), and confirmation that the legal form is a limited partnership. The general partner must sign the declaration electronically or using the secure access code. Remit the registration duty. On approval, the REQ issues the certificate of registration and assigns a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Copy of the signed partnership agreement (upon REQ request)
Identification documents for the signing general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, the REQ sends a notice of refusal or demand for clarification. Correct the inaccuracies and supply missing signatures or documents within the stated deadline, usually 10–15 days, and resubmit through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal GST/HST and Québec QST Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec – business registration services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ and partnership agreement to register the limited partnership for the federal GST/HST account with the CRA and for the Québec Sales Tax account with Revenu Québec. If the general partner is a legal person, provide its incorporation or continuity status documents and confirm the partnership's business number. Registration is generally mandatory where taxable supplies exceed the small-supplier threshold; because the catering kitchen will supply commercial air carriers, register before the first contract is performed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or Revenu Québec rejects registration due to a mismatch between the partnership name, NEQ, or registered office address, first file a corrective declaration with the REQ, then resubmit the tax registrations through the same online portals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Commercial Bank Mandate and Insurance Program
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank or credit union; insurance through an AMF-licensed broker
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a commercial bank account in the partnership's name using the registration attestation, partnership agreement, and a mandate identifying the authorized signatories. Procure general commercial liability, product liability, aviation contract liability, and property/cargo insurance. Present the general partner's resolution if the bank requires it. Ensure all account signatories have valid identification and that the bank's AML/KYC file is complete.
required_dossiers: Notarized or certified partnership agreement if required by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank returns the application because the REQ status extract is not current, retrieve an official attestation from the REQ online service and resubmit. If the insurance binder is deficient, have the broker amend the schedule and reissue the certificate within 24 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Operational Food Safety, Fire, and Municipal Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MAPAQ (Direction de l'inspection des aliments); local municipality fire prevention services; CNESST; airport authority for airside access
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the catering kitchen floor plan, equipment inventory, and HACCP plan for MAPAQ food processing permit review. Obtain a municipal building occupancy permit and arrange a fire safety inspection. For airport or airside facilities, coordinate with the airport authority for restricted-area access. Register the workplace with CNESST and implement the required health and safety prevention program before producing any meals.
required_dossiers: HACCP plan and sanitation procedure manual
Building occupancy permit application with engineer-stamped plans
Airport security access application if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MAPAQ requests further technical information, respond within 30 days with updated HACCP and microbiological control procedures. If the fire department identifies deficiencies, install the required suppression and detection systems and submit engineer-stamped drawings for reinspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) – Montréal Regional Office for international and interprovincial flight meals; Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) for the provincial food establishment
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence (Food – Manufacturing/Processing) and MAPAQ Food Processing Establishment Permit (Permis de transformation alimentaire)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCC) – Direction des évaluations environnementales
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – not listed as a mandatory environmental impact assessment activity under the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review; only municipal environmental permits and MELCC contamination-prevention compliance apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges to municipal sewers must meet local sewer by-law limits, typically pH 6.0–9.5, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, and fats, oils, and grease (FOG) ≤ 150 mg/L; grease traps are required on all food-preparation drains. Cooking exhaust must be filtered to suppress odors and particulates; cleaning products must minimize VOC emissions. Waste handling, organic waste diversion, and hazardous-residue disposal must comply with the Environment Quality Act and applicable municipal collection by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the local fire prevention service verifying means of egress, suppression systems, and evacuation planning; municipal building occupancy permit; structural load certification by a Quebec engineer for blast freezers, cooking lines, and storage racks; CNESST occupational health registration and prevention program; and, for airside kitchens, Transport Canada-compliant airport restricted-area identity pass for all ramp-delivery employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) – My Business Account portal; Revenu Québec – clicSÉQUR Affaires portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned limited partnership carrying on commercial activity in Canada/Quebec must first obtain a nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA by filing Form RC1 or using the Business Registration Online service. The BN must include the applicable program accounts, notably the GST/HST account (RT). For Quebec, the partnership must separately obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and register for QST through Revenu Québec’s clicSÉQUR Affaires portal. The registration must identify the general partner and, where a non-resident general partner acts for the LP, designate a Canadian representative and maintain books and records at an accessible Canadian address. No separate TIN/VAT ID is issued to the partnership at the federal level for income tax because the LP is tax-transparent; each partner reports its allocated share using its own BN or social insurance number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (fiscally transparent for Canadian and Quebec income tax; each limited and general partner is taxed on its allocated share of income. For GST/HST and QST, however, the partnership is itself a separate registrant and is treated as an entity-level taxpayer for indirect tax purposes).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; an LP’s pass-through status is mandatory. Relevant statutory elections for a cross-border catering LP include: (i) the GST/HST joint venture election under subsection 273(1) of the Excise Tax Act, and the corresponding QST joint venture election, to have a designated operator of an in-flight catering joint venture account for net tax as a single registrant; (ii) elections relating to nil consideration among closely related entities where applicable through corporate partners; and (iii) the hybrid mismatch rules under Canada’s BEPS Action 2 implementing legislation are mandatory, non-elective anti-avoidance provisions that deny double-deduction or deduction/non-inclusion benefits when a Quebec LP is treated as transparent in Canada but opaque in a foreign partner’s jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) administered by the CRA plus Quebec QST (Quebec Sales Tax) administered by Revenu Québec; QST is generally calculated on the same taxable base as the GST for a supply made in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter and over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters for the small-supplier threshold (both GST/HST and QST). Non-resident partnerships carrying on business in Canada may be required to register even below the threshold when they make taxable supplies in Canada in the course of a business carried on in Canada or solicit orders for tangible personal property delivered outside Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls for GST/HST or QST. Electronic tax invoices are accepted if they contain the prescribed information and are delivered in an unalterable electronic format. Revenu Québec requires QST invoices to be presented in French or in French and another language and to display the supplier’s QST registration number. The in-flight catering operation may generate invoices, warehouse uplift manifests, or EDI/API-based settlement documents, but the system must preserve an audit-ready electronic trail and permit extraction by CRA and Revenu Québec auditors. No government API clearance is required for export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating may be claimed for GST/HST and QST when the LP supplies in-flight meal trays, beverages, and cabin stores to a non-resident airline and the supplies qualify as exported supplies under subsection 23(1) of the Excise Tax Act and Schedule VI. This requires delivery at a Canadian airport onto an aircraft destined for a destination outside Canada, with the goods uplifted and removed from Canada in the course of an international flight. Related services, such as tray-up assembly, palletization, food preparation, and ramp delivery performed for the non-resident airline, are also zero-rated where the tangible personal property is exported or the service is supplied to a non-resident and the benefit is realized outside Canada. Domestic-flight catering, ground meals, crew meals consumed in Canada, and supplies to Canadian-resident entities are taxable at the combined 14.975% rate unless a separate zero-rating provision applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A filed electronically through the Canadian Goods Exported Reporting System (CERS) or an equivalent electronic export declaration where the CBSA requires reporting of uplifted aviation stores)

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / Flight Manifest (master airway bill, cargo manifest, or airline uplift manifest identifying the flight number, destination airport, departure date, and catering load quantity)
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/FX statement showing settlement received from the non-resident airline and the repatriation of exchange proceeds to Canada
Catering uplift/delivery receipt signed by the aircraft captain or airline handling agent, including the flight number, route, meal count, and CBSA confirmation where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess a zero-rating claim within the normal four-year reassessment period, and without limitation where a misrepresentation is attributable to fraud, wilful default, or gross negligence. Civil penalties for knowingly making a false or misleading tax statement include a penalty of up to 25% of the tax or net tax sought to be evaded, plus arrears interest and refusal of input tax credits. Revenu Québec applies parallel QST penalties under Quebec sales tax legislation. Tax evasion prosecution can lead to fines of up to 200% of the evaded amount and imprisonment. A successful audit clawback is retroactive to the original supply date, zero-rating refunds and rebates are repaid with interest, and the partnership’s general and limited partners may be jointly and severally liable for the partnership’s GST/HST and QST liabilities while partners.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority of Canada; Payments Canada operates the national clearing and settlement infrastructure (Large Value Transfer System transitioning to the ISO 20022 Lynx service, and the Automated Clearing Settlement System); the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) conducts prudential supervision of Canadian chartered banks and federal financial institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and monitors cross-border electronic fund transfers; in Quebec, the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) supervises provincial financial services, insurance, and securities distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible with no general government exchange-control regime; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951 and Canada observes Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. Current-account transactions (trade settlement, raw food imports, packaging, equipment leases) and capital-account movements (non-resident LP capital contributions, partner remittance, loan repayments, acquisition of foreign assets) are unrestricted. Profit remittance obstacles are tax-based, not FX-based: a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) must allocate business income to partners via the T5013 Partnership Information Return and the Quebec Relevé 15; non-resident limited partners are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act on their share of Canadian-source business income through the LP, and distributions are not subject to Part XIII withholding unless they represent interest, royalties, rent, guarantee, or management fees, in which case Part XIII withholding of up to 25% applies unless reduced by an applicable Canada tax treaty. Quebec-specific taxation under the Taxation Act (Quebec) and Revenu Québec filing obligations apply in parallel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender rules, no repatriation timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Inflight catering receipts invoiced to foreign airlines may be retained in USD or other foreign currencies indefinitely for working capital purposes. The applicable obligations are: (i) FINTRAC reporting by the bank of every international electronic funds transfer of CAD 10,000 or more (or equivalent); (ii) complete recordkeeping of export transactions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and the Safe Food for Canadians Regulations; (iii) if foreign receipts are held offshore, the LP must reflect the amounts in Canadian financial statements and in the T5013/Relevé 15 capital account reconciliation, and the partners must consider the foreign accrual property income rules and attribution rules under the Income Tax Act.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Primary Operational Account (CAD and USD) with segregated LP Capital Contribution Sub-Account
Capital Escrow Account and Zero-Balance Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Group (Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Receivables Concentration Account with Monthly ACH Settlement Capability
Operational Account with Trade Finance and Documentary Letter of Credit Facility
Operational Account with Treasury Management and FX Forward Execution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury and capital escrow facilities; Medium for ancillary cross-border disbursement rails. The Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46) restricts deposit-taking in Canada to authorized banks; offshore digital EMIs and e-money institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex, and similar platforms) generally do not hold a Canadian banking licence and cannot lawfully accept the Quebec LP's deposits as their own liabilities. A legally viable structure restricts fintech use to a non-depository payments facility where the EMI is a FINTRAC-registered money services business (MSB) and the LP is identified as the ultimate beneficial owner; such rails may handle low-value, high-frequency supplier disbursements and cross-border crew or contractor payments, but all inbound capital contributions and the end-of-day cash sweep must settle to a Schedule I bank account or an authorized Canadian foreign bank branch.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The PCMLTFA Regulations do not mandate an in-branch physical appearance for corporate account opening; electronic identity verification of authorized signatories is legally permitted. In practice, Schedule I banks require: (i) a live video KYC interview with the authorized signatories and, for most files, the ultimate beneficial owners holding 25% or more; (ii) valid government-issued identification of every director of the corporate general partner; (iii) a notarized or legalized certification of the LP deed and general partner resolutions; and (iv) an in-person appointment at a Quebec branch or an approved foreign representative office where the partnership is new to the bank. The Quebec limited partnership must supply its attestation of immatriculation and enterprise number (NEQ) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). A fully remote opening is possible only under a dual-verification procedure (video interview plus bank-to-bank confirmation), and the account will be transaction-limited until original or certified documents are delivered by courier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership structure, including a non-resident corporate general partner or nominee layers above the Quebec LP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organizational chart identifying each ultimate individual beneficial owner and each 25% or greater interest; certified copy of the limited partnership agreement and contribution schedules; REQ attestation of immatriculation and certificate of good standing for the corporate general partner; executed corporate resolutions naming each signatory and confirming authority; beneficial ownership declaration compliant with PCMLTFA core requirements; negative statement on bearer shares, custodial arrangements, or nominee fiduciary holdings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding or intercompany wires that mask the source of the LP capital contribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements and financial statements of each contributing limited partner; executed capital commitment and subscription agreement; source-of-wealth questionnaire covering earnings, liquidation events, or enterprise dispositions; express representation that contributed funds are not derived from criminal proceeds and were not structured to avoid the CAD 10,000 FINTRAC reporting threshold; intercompany loan agreements and evidence of arm's-length debt terms where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, adverse media, or counterparty risk in the airline, catering, or food-supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party due diligence runs (World-Check, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, or equivalent) on the LP and all material counterparties; radar screening against Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; customs and bonded-warehouse documentation for airport catering goods; HACCP plan and Safe Food for Canadians Regulations licence; Transport Canada and CATSA airport restricted-area credential records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners resident in high-risk or FATF grey-list jurisdictions, creating disproportional geopolitical and financial-crime exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report on each non-resident partner; current tax residence certificates; independent verification of economic substance in the partner's home jurisdiction; written commercial rationale for the partnership investment; evidence that the partner's committed capital is sourced from the partner's own tax-filed financial institutions; presentation to the bank's financial crimes committee for a client-specific risk treatment decision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity inconsistent with inflight catering operations, including rapid payment reversals or pattern resembling invoice discounting or remittance services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoice-level sales ledger matched against airline purchase orders and signed delivery records; executed inflight catering master service agreement; supplier contracts and purchase orders for raw food, packaging, and transport; treasury dashboard proving that aviation contract wires and monthly ACH receipts correlate with agreed billing cycles; auditor confirmation of meal production volumes and distribution economics.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from non-resident limited partners are routed by SWIFT MT103 to the LP's Canadian bank account; the domestic CAD leg clears through Payments Canada's high-value system (LVTS, transitioning to Lynx with ISO 20022). The MT103 must state the full legal name of the LP, the account number, and an explicit purpose description such as 'LP capital contribution under limited partnership agreement dated [date]' so the beneficiary bank can match the wire to the KYC profile. Canada imposes no foreign-exchange control purpose codes, but the bank will require the subscription agreement and source-of-funds evidence for each contribution of CAD 10,000 or more. USD-denominated contributions may be converted to CAD at the bank's spot rate or held in a USD sub-account at the LP's election; no forced conversion applies. The inbound contribution is a capital account movement and is not taxable, but the capital schedule must be updated for the T5013 and Quebec Relevé 15 reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements are segregated by clearing rail: (i) international supplier payments for food commodities and packaging are executed by SWIFT MT103 with 48-hour payee validation, supported by purchase orders and commodity contracts; (ii) capital acquisitions of kitchen equipment (blast chillers, tray assembly lines, water purification systems) are settled by documentary irrevocable letters of credit (MT700) with usance drafts, supported by invoice, bill of lading, and customs entry; (iii) recurring low-value payments to Quebec and Canadian suppliers migrate to the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) as monthly ACH pre-authorized transfer files; (iv) USD-denominated airline revenue is received via Fedwire or CHIPS into the USD liquidity account and swept to the CAD operational account under a standing FX netting instruction; (v) for IATA member airline counterparties, the LP may present catering invoices through the IATA Clearing House (ICH) for net monthly settlement in the agreed currency, reducing wire count and counterparty settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts in CAD/USD with tenors from 1 to 12 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; permitted without exchange-control approval because Canada imposes no restrictions on corporate FX forward transactions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for limited-liquidity currency pairs used when a foreign airline or supplier settles in a non-deliverable currency; permitted solely when documented as a hedge of contractual revenue or payable exposure and subject to the bank's internal counterparty limits.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD/USD) for long-dated capital facility financing or for hedging the USD-denominated capex and airline contract mix; permitted under the same ISDA/CSA master agreement for non-financial counterparties.
Vanilla European-style OTC FX options in CAD/USD, including zero-cost collars and participating forwards, to hedge asymmetric monthly invoice flows from foreign-domiciled airlines.
FX swaps (swap points) for short-term funding liquidity and same-week working capital smoothing across the CAD and USD accounts, restricted to non-speculative treasury operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle des sociétés) filed by the partnership under the Québec Business Corporations Act or the Civil Code of Québec partnership registration regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Registraire d'entreprises du Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing must be completed no later than the anniversary date of registration each year; a grace period is not provided by statute
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 10 per day to a maximum of CAD 200 for annual declarations; prolonged default leads to administrative dissolution or strike-off by the Registraire des entreprises

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal return of partnership income (T5013 Summary and T5013 Information Return) for the limited partnership's fiscal period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the later of March 31 following the calendar year or the date that is five months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 for late filing; additional penalties under Income Tax Act and potential loss of capacity to claim certain deductions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec partnership income declaration (Relevé 15 / CO-17 related schedules) where the limited partnership carries on business or has Québec-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the same deadline applicable to the federal T5013 return, generally March 31 or five months after fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties and interest on any unpaid amounts; repeated default can trigger collection measures and administrative enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal corporate income tax return for each corporate general partner where the T5013 allocation is reported (T2 return for the partner, not the partnership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the corporate partner's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; repeated failure may result in criminal prosecution or director liability assessments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Québec enterprise registration annual update confirming registered office, general partner identity, and partnership activity code (NAICS 722310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the registration anniversary; any change to registered office or general partners must be filed within 60 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative late penalty of CAD 10 per day up to CAD 200; failure to maintain accurate registration can lead to revocation of the enterprise's registration and loss of legal capacity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit under the Civil Code of Québec or the Québec Business Corporations Act for a limited partnership itself, provided it does not have securities listed on a recognized stock exchange and does not fall under financial institution legislation; audit requirements may arise contractually, through the limited partnership agreement, or where a corporate general partner is a reporting issuer. An audit may also be required under federal or provincial anti-money laundering rules if the catering operation is a non-financial business and the annual gross revenue exceeds CAD 10,000 in cannabis-related dealings, which is inapplicable to standard airline catering.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board is required for publicly accountable enterprises; private limited partnerships with no public accountability may elect IFRS or the Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE). Financial statements should follow the CPA Canada Handbook and, in Québec, may require compliance with the legal accounting provisions of the Civil Code of Québec.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Federal and Québec corporate statutes do not require a publicly accessible annual UBO re-confirmation filing for a limited partnership; however, the Registraire des entreprises requires annual confirmation of the general partner and any registrable ultimate beneficiary where the partnership is registered in the enterprise register. Changes in partners, including transfers of limited partnership interests, must be declared to the Registraire des entreprises within 60 days of the change. The partnership must maintain internal books and records of all persons who hold limited partnership interests and any individuals who directly or indirectly control at least 25% of the partnership interests, subject to access under applicable anti-money laundering and tax administration powers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 8,000 to CAD 25,000 per year for a certified independent audit if required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: LP pass-through (0% entity-level); federal general corporate rate 15%; Quebec general rate 11.5%; combined 26.5% for non-CCPC corporate partners
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner: federal 9% small business deduction on first CAD 500,000 of active business income plus Quebec reduced rate 3.2%, combined 12.2%; income allocated to a non-resident corporate partner remains eligible for treaty business profits only if no Quebec permanent establishment. Available preferences include accelerated capital cost allowance on food-processing equipment, SR&ED investment tax credits, and Quebec tax credit for manufacturing/food processing; no partnership-level holiday applies.
